note: A tylosin-class 16-membered macrolide (larger than the erythromycin-class scaffold suggested in the main fixture file's macrocycle-design row). Deliberately not analyzed or measured in this RFC round -- reserved to check A1's eventual measurement methodology (and, later, A2's ensemble design) against a macrocycle it was not designed against. Per this project's established holdout discipline (e.g. round 2C-3's hypoxanthine holdout, checked only after the design was frozen), do not use this molecule to shape A1/A2's design; check it only after.

A cyclic hexapeptide scaffold (verified via RDKit to parse and form a genuine macrocyclic ring, formula not independently cross-checked against a named natural product -- treat as a synthetic representative of the flexible-cyclic-peptide class, not a specific compound). Reserved the same way as oe-holdout-01: not used to shape A1/A2, checked only after design is frozen.

A flexible drug-like molecule (imidazobenzene + piperazine linker) with multiple rotatable bonds but no macrocycle and no exotic atom types -- a 'should be easy' case for A2's eventual seed-reproducibility and energy-ranking acceptance criteria. Reserved to confirm A2's design generalizes beyond the specific failure-mode molecule (the halomethane [C@H](F)(Cl)Br case, oe-01's own decane repro having since been found not to reproduce on current main) used to diagnose the defect in the main fixture file, not fit to it.

Palmitic acid: a long, highly flexible acyclic chain -- the class of molecule where best-of-N energy-ranked selection should matter most (many similar-RMSD, different-energy conformers). Reserved the same way as the other holdout rows: not used to shape A2's best-of-N design, checked only after A2's methodology is frozen, to confirm the eventual energy-ranking step actually discriminates on a case built to need it.
